subject: Planned rolling driver swap in eu-west-2 — brief window and customer impact
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.ai>
To: BrightWave Ops <ops@brightwave.com>, Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@retail-matrix.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-20T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: Planned rolling driver swap in eu-west-2 — brief window and customer impact

Hi Maria / BrightWave team,

Quick heads-up: we have a scheduled, staggered driver swap across the eu-west-2 serving cluster that will start on May 21 at 02:00 UTC and finish no later than 06:00 UTC. This is a rolling operation (node-by-node) designed to replace a NIC/driver revision that addresses packet loss seen in microbursts at high token throughput.

What to expect for BrightWave:
- No API key changes or client configuration required.
- Minimal single-request latency spikes (~250–500ms) during the small switchover on a node.
- We will drain active sessions per node prior to restart; persistent streaming connections may reconnect to a different regional replica.
- We do not expect request failures, but we will temporarily route traffic to warm pools if an eviction occurs.

Action items for you (recommended, optional):
1) If you run long-lived streaming sessions, plan to tolerate a one-time reconnect during the 02:00–06:00 UTC window.
2) If you have a maintenance blackout policy, tell us ASAP and we can schedule a narrow exception.

Attachments: driver-update-checklist.pdf (runbook extract), maintenance-runbook-v2.docx

We will post live updates to status.redwood.ai and provide a brief postmortem within 48 hours. Jordan and Neha are on the ops rotation and will monitor the window.

Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Customer Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
sofia@redwood.ai

Thanks Sofia — appreciated. A couple quick clarifications:
1) Our streaming checkout service maintains long-lived SSE connections. If those reconnect, will session affinity be preserved or will they land on a different replica?
2) Do you expect any transient rate-limit spikes that we should pre-adjust on our side?

We do not have a blackout window, so the timing works for us. We will monitor and report anything abnormal.

— Ben (BrightWave Ops)

Ben / BrightWave / Sofia — answering Ben's questions:
- Session affinity: our L7 load balancer preserves client affinity by cookie/IP for active sessions, but during a node drain the streaming connection will be closed and the client will re-establish. The new connection will usually land on a different warm replica; session tokens are stateless so reconnection should be seamless.
- Rate-limit behavior: we will temporarily increase the per-account token-rate headroom on the orchestration layer for the 02:00–08:00 UTC period by +15% to allow reconnect storms. No action needed from BrightWave unless you rely on very tight rate-limit windows.

I'll be on the rotation during the window and Marissa will coordinate logs and telemetry export. We will update the Status page and paste a short Slack summary in #customers-brightwave.

Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Post-maintenance confirmation & next steps — eu-west-2 driver swap completed

Hi Maria / Ben,

Short update: the rolling driver swap completed at 05:42 UTC with all nodes transitioned and no customer-visible errors reported in our monitoring. Highlights:
- No API errors for BrightWave during the window.
- We saw brief latency tail spikes (median +180ms, p99 +420ms) on a small subset of requests during single-node evacuations — within our expected bounds.
- One streaming reconnect count increased for BrightWave by ~0.6% during the window; Jordan confirmed those sessions rejoined successfully.

Next steps (what you'll see):
- We will publish a short postmortem doc and telemetry extracts to the drive link below within 36 hours.
- If you would like a shared walk-through of the telemetry, we can set a 30-minute readout next week.

Post-maintenance artifacts: postmortem-template.md (attached), detailed runbook + telemetry: https://drive.redwood.ai/teams/ops/2026/euw2-driver-swap-runbook

Thanks for the quick coordination and for flagging streaming sensitivity earlier. If anything is off on your side, reply here and we'll prioritize.

Best,
Sofia
